our_text: This claim is false. No FDA law allows human meat in food—it's illegal. The "6%" comes from a 2016 Clear Labs study finding 6% of burgers had wrong animal meat (e.g., chicken instead of beef). Human DNA was found in just 1 of 258 samples, from handler contact, not meat. https://www.businessinsider.com/burger-report-finds-substitutions-contaminants-2016-5
helpful_text: The FDA does not allow any human meat or DNA in food. The "6%" claim misinterprets a 2016 study finding trace human DNA (likely from hair/skin during handling) in one burger sample, not meat or an allowance. Human meat in fast food claims are hoaxes.    https://www.truevaluemetrics.org/DBpdfs/Food/ClearLabs/ClearLabs-Hamburger-Report-2016.pdf https://apnews.com/article/archive-fact-checking-9233643423 https://www.reuters.com/article/fact-check/mcdonalds-human-meat-claims-stem-from-sati

our_text: Cancer is caused by genetic mutations and cellular dysregulation, not parasites. While ivermectin and fenbendazole are being researched, no clinical trials have proven they cure cancer in humans. These remain experimental, not established treatments. https://www.cancer.gov/about-cancer/understanding/what-is-cancer
helpful_text: Cancer is not parasites, though some parasitic infections can increase the risk of certain cancers. our_text: Devil's Tower is a confirmed igneous rock formation made of phonolite porphyry, not a petrified tree. No root system was discovered—this claim originated from a satirical fake news site. helpful_text: Devils Tower is an igneous rock formation from cooled magma, not a petrified tree. Claims of seismic readings showing a root system come from a 2017 satirical post and are false. Columns formed by jointing as magma cooled.    https://www.usgs.gov/geology-and-ecology-of-national-parks/devils-tower-national-monument  https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/roots-devils-tower  https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2021/jul/08/facebook-posts/devils-tower-rock-formation-despite-wrong-recycled/
